subject: math.DG
name: Hopf’s Euler-characteristic conjecture
statement: Must every closed even-dimensional Riemannian manifold with strictly positive sectional curvature have positive Euler characteristic?
importance: It asks for a fundamental topological consequence of positive sectional curvature.
status_note: The assertion is known in low dimensions and under additional symmetry assumptions, but not in all even dimensions.

subject: math.DG
name: Hopf’s product conjecture
statement: Can S^2 × S^2 carry any Riemannian metric with strictly positive sectional curvature?
importance: This basic product is a decisive test of the scarcity of positively curved manifolds.
status_note: The conjectured answer is no; nonnegative sectional curvature is easy to obtain, and stronger curvature conditions are different questions.

subject: math.DG
name: Bott’s rational ellipticity conjecture
statement: Is every closed simply connected Riemannian manifold with nonnegative sectional curvature rationally elliptic, meaning its total rational homotopy is finite-dimensional?
importance: It predicts a strong restriction on the homotopy complexity permitted by nonnegative curvature.
status_note: The simply connected and closed hypotheses are part of the statement; many symmetric examples satisfy it, but the general case is open.

references.title: Torus orbifolds, slice-maximal torus actions and rational ellipticity

subject: math.DG
name: Markus conjecture
statement: Is every compact connected affine manifold whose flat torsion-free affine connection admits a parallel volume form geodesically complete?
importance: It seeks a geometric characterization of completeness using volume preservation.
status_note: Completeness implies the existence of a parallel volume form in the compact setting; the reverse implication is open in general and known in several special cases.

references.title: Affine manifolds and the Markus conjecture

subject: math.DG
name: Goldberg conjecture in negative scalar curvature
statement: Must every compact Einstein almost-Kähler manifold with negative scalar curvature have an integrable almost-complex structure, and hence be Kähler?
importance: It asks whether an Einstein metric forces an almost-Kähler structure to become complex geometry.
status_note: The compact nonnegative-scalar-curvature case is proved; noncompact counterexamples do not settle this remaining compact case.

references.title: On some compact Einstein almost Kähler manifolds

subject: math.DG
name: Chern’s minimal-hypersurface conjecture
statement: For each n, is the set of constant values of |A|^2 attained by closed minimal hypersurfaces in the unit sphere S^(n+1) discrete, where A is the second fundamental form?
importance: It predicts a gap structure for the curvature of minimal hypersurfaces.
status_note: The hypersurface is required to have constant scalar curvature, equivalently constant |A|^2; initial gap results do not settle discreteness of the full set.

subject: math.DG
name: Bartnik splitting conjecture
statement: Must a spatially compact globally hyperbolic spacetime that is timelike geodesically complete and satisfies Ric(v,v) at least zero for every timelike vector v be isometric to a static product (R × Σ, −dt^2 + h)?
importance: It tests whether a nonsingular cosmology satisfying the timelike convergence condition must be static.
status_note: The Lorentzian splitting theorem applies when a complete timelike line exists; producing such a line under these hypotheses is the unresolved step.

references.title: Achronal limits, Lorentzian spheres, and splitting

subject: math.DG
name: Gromov’s macroscopic-dimension conjecture
statement: For every closed n-dimensional manifold with a positive-scalar-curvature metric, does its universal cover have macroscopic dimension at most n−2, meaning it admits a uniformly cobounded map to an (n−2)-dimensional simplicial complex?
importance: It connects scalar curvature with the large-scale topology of universal covers.
status_note: Many group and spin cases are established; the unrestricted statement for closed positive-scalar-curvature manifolds remains open.

references.title: Positive Scalar Curvature, Macroscopic Dimension, and Inessential Manifolds

subject: math.DG
name: Willmore minimization in genus two
statement: Determine the exact infimum of the Willmore energy integral H^2 dA over smooth closed embedded genus-two surfaces in R^3, and classify all minimizers up to conformal transformations.
importance: It is the next fundamental surface-energy problem after the sphere and torus cases.
status_note: Existence and bounds are known; the genus-one minimum is 2π^2 by Marques–Neves, while the exact genus-two minimum is unresolved.

subject: math.DG
name: General Penrose inequality
statement: For asymptotically flat three-dimensional initial data with a complete exterior up to the horizon for Einstein’s equations satisfying the dominant energy condition and having a connected outermost future apparent horizon, must the ADM mass m be at least sqrt(A_min/(16π)), where A_min is the infimum of the areas of smooth closed surfaces enclosing that horizon?
importance: It relates black-hole horizon geometry to total mass and tests cosmic censorship quantitatively.
status_note: The time-symmetric Riemannian case is proved; the general case with nonzero second fundamental form is open. Using the apparent-horizon area itself rather than the least-area enclosure gives a false variant.

references.title: The Penrose inequality and apparent horizons
